chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Yusuf ibn Aqeel, from his father, from Musa ibn Habeeb, from Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said:
Allah does not Sanctify a community in which there is clanging by the clarets and its eulogies cause grief.

key_terms.بَرْبَط: A musical instrument, often identified as a lute or clarinet, used in pre-Islamic and early Islamic times.
key_terms.تَائِه: A type of drum or musical instrument, often associated with mourning or grief.
key_terms.تُفَجِّعُ: Causing grief or sorrow, indicating the emotional impact of the instrument's sound.
key_terms.يُقَعْقِعُ: Clanging or making a loud noise, referring to the sound of the instrument.

ai.seo_question: What does the term 'barbat' refer to in Shia hadith regarding music?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) to link specific musical instruments to the spiritual degradation of a community. Shia scholars, such as Allama al-Majlisi, interpret 'barbat' and 'ta'ih' not merely as generic instruments but as symbols of frivolity and sorrow that distract the heart from divine remembrance, thereby preventing Allah from bestowing sanctification (taqdis) upon the society.
